clue.text: He's looked over by an employer

parts.note: per means by, as in 'per post'
a user is one who employs something, such as a tool

explanation.surface: A worker gets inspected by the boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He's looked over' reads as passive, but it means 'he has looked over': one who reads through something.
explanation.definitionFit: A reader who scans a document carefully is said to peruse it.

clue.text: An individual flattening reporters with little hesitation

parts.note: the press is the body of reporters
er is the short sound of hesitating

explanation.surface: Someone crushing journalists with barely a pause.
explanation.definitionFit: One who presses clothes or metal smooths it flat.

clue.text: Though somewhat eccentric, he's the most prosperous

indicators.note: somewhat means only a part of the following words is used

explanation.surface: An odd character turns out to be the wealthiest man around.
explanation.definitionFit: Being prosperous means having wealth, so the superlative is the wealthiest.

clue.text: Teams being changed around account for a draw

indicators.note: around says the rearranged letters surround the other piece
being changed says the letters of the word before are rearranged

parts.note: a tale is an account or story

explanation.surface: A reshuffle of the teams explains why the match was drawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being changed' signals the anagram, and 'around' says the shuffled teams wrap the account; 'draw' here is a drawn game in chess.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess a position with no legal move is a drawn game.

clue.text: Upright, but not well-behaved

explanation.surface: Standing tall yet badly behaved.
explanation.definitionFit: In heraldry a beast rearing on its hind legs is so described; the everyday sense is unrestrained or unruly.

clue.text: Where to see a large bird at the water-side

indicators.note: at places the bird beside the water

parts.note: a swan is a large water bird
the sea is a body of water, and this one is at the side of a Welsh city

explanation.surface: Instructions on where to spot a big bird by the shore.
explanation.walkthrough: SWANSEA is a coastal city in South Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: A Welsh seaside city is a place, answering the question 'where'.

clue.text: Grave foreign coppers holding back anger

indicators.note: holding says one piece contains the other

parts.note: sous are small French coins, copper money abroad

indicators.note: back says the word for anger is read backwards

parts.note: ire is anger

explanation.surface: Serious-faced overseas police restrain their fury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' signals reversing the word for anger. 'Coppers' suggests police but means copper coins, here French ones.
explanation.definitionFit: A grave expression is a solemn, earnest one.

clue.text: Such a plea is out of place

definitions.text: Such a plea is out of place

parts.words: Such a plea is out of place
parts.note: a defence claiming the accused was elsewhere at the time of the crime, literally 'in another place'

explanation.definitionFit: The Latin word means elsewhere, and the defence pleads absence from the scene.

clue.text: Ineffectual step taken to shelter royalty

indicators.note: taken to shelter means the step encloses the royal letters

parts.note: a stile is a step for climbing over a fence
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: A useless stairway is built to protect the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Something barren produces no result, so it is fruitless.

clue.text: Go-ahead branches

parts.note: read as branches that go on a head, like a deer's horns, not enterprising offices

explanation.definitionFit: A stag's horns are branched growths on its head.

clue.text: Call late with application

parts.note: ex means former or late, as in ex-husband
a claim is an application, as for benefits

explanation.surface: A request to phone made after hours with a form.
explanation.definitionFit: To call out is to cry out suddenly.

clue.text: The intention in regular payment for clothes

indicators.note: in places the intention inside the payment

parts.note: rent is paid regularly
an aim is an intention

explanation.surface: Someone sets aside a monthly sum for their wardrobe.
explanation.definitionFit: An old literary word for garments or attire.

clue.text: View only part of the play

explanation.surface: Seeing just a portion of a theatrical performance.
explanation.definitionFit: A scene can be a vista or landscape, and also a division of an act in drama.

clue.text: An Australian, one with spirit, interrupting a bore

indicators.note: interrupting means breaking into the middle of the other piece

parts.note: a bore, as written, a tedious person
I is the Roman numeral one
gin is a spirit

explanation.surface: An Aussie with a drink cuts in on a tedious talker.
explanation.walkthrough: IGIN goes into ABORE after its R: ABOR-IGIN-E.
explanation.definitionFit: An indigenous inhabitant of Australia.

clue.text: Plot after military personnel withdraw

indicators.note: after puts the plot behind the military letters

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
a tract is a plot or area of land

explanation.surface: Soldiers pull back from a scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plot' looks like a scheme but is a piece of land.
explanation.definitionFit: To retract a statement is to take it back.

clue.text: In the main one finds them strangely ageless

definitions.text: In the main one finds them

indicators.note: strangely means the letters of the following word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something mysteriously timeless is found at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The main' is an old poetic word for the open sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailors develop the ability to keep their balance on a rolling ship.

clue.text: A person keeping old papers put the most important four first

parts.note: arch means chief, as in archbishop
IV is the Roman numeral four
1st, written IST, means first

explanation.surface: A records clerk sorts priorities by putting the top four ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' looks like an instruction to place something earlier, but it is written as 1ST, with I for the 1.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who maintains historical records and documents.

clue.text: Stick up for enterprise

explanation.surface: Make a stand in support of a business venture.
explanation.definitionFit: To jut out is to protrude, and a planned undertaking is a scheme.

clue.text: Composing short page about former ecclesiastic head

parts.note: p is the abbreviation for page
re means about or concerning
late means former, as in the late chairman

explanation.surface: Writing a brief note about a former church leader.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop or other senior cleric of the church.

clue.text: Ace with sour disposition and very hard

parts.note: an ace counts as one

indicators.note: disposition, as an arrangement, says the letters of sour are rearranged

explanation.surface: A top player with a grumpy temperament makes life tough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disposition' looks like temperament but signals rearranging SOUR into ROUS.
explanation.definitionFit: A burdensome task is one that is very demanding.

clue.text: The use of three banks ensured progress in this craft

definitions.text: The use of three banks ensured progress in this craft

parts.words: The use of three banks ensured progress in this craft
parts.note: banks here are tiers of oars on an ancient warship, not financial institutions

explanation.definitionFit: A Greek galley was rowed with oars on three levels.

clue.text: Firm figure, the top man, when preparing to do some firing!

parts.note: co is short for company, a firm
C is the Roman numeral one hundred
a king is the top man

explanation.surface: A business boss readies the guns.
explanation.definitionFit: Raising a gun's hammer readies it to shoot.

clue.text: Horseman given small coin (gold) right?

parts.note: a cent is a small coin
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A rider is paid a small gold coin, correct?
explanation.definitionFit: In myth, a creature half man and half horse.

clue.text: Letter opening

explanation.surface: Opening a piece of correspondence.
explanation.definitionFit: A first letter of a name, and also something first or beginning.

clue.text: Dogs possibly stop being regarded as a heavenly gift

indicators.note: possibly says the letters of dogs could be arranged another way

parts.note: an end is a stop

explanation.surface: Pets might stop being thought of as a blessing.
explanation.definitionFit: A welcome blessing that seems sent from above.

clue.text: Being promoted, given no leave — it's quite wrong

indicators.note: quite wrong says the letters are put in a different order

parts.note: the it of it's; the 's adds no letter

explanation.surface: Getting a promotion without any holiday is unfair.
explanation.definitionFit: Being raised to a higher rank is advancement.

clue.text: Lounge appropriated by an outsider

indicators.note: appropriated by means taken in by the other piece

parts.note: to lie is to lounge

explanation.surface: A sitting room is taken over by a stranger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lounge' looks like a room but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A foreigner or stranger is a person from outside.

clue.text: A story of heroes coming back in all the national dailies

indicators.note: coming back says the letters are taken in reverse order
in says the letters are found inside the word

explanation.surface: Tales of champions return in all the newspapers.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer's epic poem about the Trojan War and its warriors.

clue.text: Subject to suffering, lives in past

indicators.note: in puts the lives word inside the past word

parts.note: agone is an archaic word for past or ago
is means exists or lives

explanation.surface: Someone suffers while living in the past.
explanation.definitionFit: To torment oneself or another is to cause anguish.

clue.text: A popular egghead about to commit a crime — so foolish

indicators.note: about means the first pieces go around the other

parts.note: in means popular, fashionable
E is the head, first letter, of egg
to sin is to commit a wrong

explanation.surface: A well-liked intellectual about to break the law is silly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'egghead' looks like an intellectual but gives E. AINE goes around SIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Silly or stupid, literally like a donkey.

clue.text: Fundamental nature of sense as may be seen by the church

indicators.note: by places the church letters next to the anagram
as may be seen suggests the word sense viewed in another arrangement

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: The core of good sense as the church sees it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as may be seen' shuffles SENSE to ESSEN.
explanation.definitionFit: The intrinsic quality that makes a thing what it is.

clue.text: Made a din and caused annoyance

explanation.surface: Making noise and being irritating.
explanation.definitionFit: It means clattered noisily, and also unsettled or irritated someone.
